q21884.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of a mobile worksite with a narrowing on the left.

explain.short: The red line shows the left lane closing and the triangle shows works ahead: a mobile worksite with a narrowing on the left.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'strettoia a sinistra' (narrowing on the left) matches the red line on the LEFT.

sceneParams.caption: Mobile works: left lane closes in 500 m

q21885.en: The sign shown can be mounted on a vehicle to give advance warning of roadworks.

explain.short: For moving works, this panel is often carried by a vehicle that drives behind the workers to warn traffic.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'può essere installato su un veicolo' is right: a mobile worksite moves, so its sign moves too.

sceneParams.caption: This panel can ride on a works vehicle

q21886.en: The sign shown indicates the lanes available for traffic.

explain.short: The black arrows show the lanes that stay open; the red line shows the lane that closes.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'corsie disponibili' (available lanes) = the black arrows.

sceneParams.caption: Black arrows = lanes still open

q21887.en: The sign shown indicates a reduction from three lanes to two.

explain.short: The panel has three lanes: the left one (red) ends and two black arrows continue.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: Count the lanes: three at the bottom, two at the top ('da tre a due').

sceneParams.caption: Three lanes become two

q21888.en: The sign shown can be fitted with flashing yellow lights.

explain.short: The two round lamps on top of the panel are flashing yellow lights, so drivers see it from far away.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: Look at the two round lamps at the top: 'luci gialle lampeggianti' are allowed and common.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow lights make it visible

q21889.en: The sign shown indicates how many vehicles may pass at the same time.

explain.short: The arrows are lanes, not vehicles: the sign shows which lanes are open, not a number of vehicles.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'quanti veicoli' (how many vehicles) is wrong: arrows show lanes, not a vehicle count.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows = open lanes, not number of cars

q21890.en: The sign shown indicates a lay-by on the left side.

explain.short: The red line on the left is a lane closed for works, not a place to stop.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary sign) warns of a mobile worksite (cantiere mobile): of three lanes, the left one closes (red line) and two stay open (black arrows). It can be mounted on a works vehicle and fitted with flashing yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is wrong: red = lane closed, not parking.

sceneParams.caption: Left lane closed for works, not a lay-by

q21891.en: The sign shown tells vehicles with an actual mass over 7 tonnes heading to Lucca to change route.

explain.short: The 7 t ban sits on the straight arrow to Lucca, so heavier vehicles going to Lucca must take another road.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'massa effettiva' (actual mass) over 7 t: only these vehicles must change route.

sceneParams.caption: Over 7 t to Lucca: take the detour

q21892.en: The sign shown allows lorries with a fully laden mass under 7 tonnes to continue straight on.

explain.short: The ban covers only vehicles over 7 t; a lorry under 7 t even when fully loaded is never over 7 t, so it may go straight.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'inferiore a 7 tonnellate' (under 7 t): the ban does not touch these lorries.

sceneParams.caption: Under 7 t: straight on to Lucca is fine

q21893.en: The sign shown does not allow vehicles with an actual mass over 7 tonnes heading to Lucca to continue straight on.

explain.short: The 7 t ban circle is right on the straight arrow to Lucca.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'non consente ... di proseguire diritto' is correct, but only for the heavy vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Over 7 t: no straight on to Lucca

q21894.en: The sign shown indicates a traffic restriction on a stretch of road for vehicles with an actual mass over 7 tonnes.

explain.short: The road straight ahead is closed only to vehicles over 7 t, for example because of the works.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'limitazione di transito' (traffic restriction): it limits only the heavy vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Stretch ahead closed to vehicles over 7 t

q21895.en: The sign shown is placed near a junction that comes before a roadworks site.

explain.short: It is a yellow direction panel: it stands before the junction where heavy vehicles must leave the route closed by the works.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'in vicinanza di un incrocio' (near a junction) is right: you need a junction to change route.

sceneParams.caption: Placed before the junction, ahead of the works

q21896.en: The sign shown is one of the temporary signs for roadworks sites.

explain.short: Its yellow background tells you it is a temporary sign used for roadworks.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: Yellow background = temporary ('segnali temporanei').

sceneParams.caption: Yellow background = temporary works sign

q21897.en: The sign shown tells all vehicles that they cannot continue straight on to Lucca.

explain.short: Only vehicles over 7 t are stopped; all others may go straight on to Lucca.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'a tutti i veicoli' (to all vehicles) is wrong: the ban is only for vehicles over 7 t.

sceneParams.caption: Only over 7 t must change route, not everyone

q21898.en: The sign shown requires all vehicles to turn right at the next fork.

explain.short: Nobody is forced to turn: only vehicles over 7 t must leave the straight route to Lucca.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'obbliga tutti i veicoli' (requires all vehicles) is wrong: it concerns only vehicles over 7 t.

sceneParams.caption: Not all must turn: only over 7 t change route

q21899.en: The sign shown forbids overtaking for motor vehicles with a total mass over 7 tonnes.

explain.short: It is about which road to take, not about overtaking: heavy vehicles may not go straight on to Lucca.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: 'vieta il sorpasso' (no overtaking) is wrong: it is a transit ban on one route.

sceneParams.caption: Route ban for over 7 t, not an overtaking ban

q21900.en: The sign shown forbids access to vehicles longer than 7 metres.

explain.short: The circle says '7 t': tonnes of mass, not metres of length.
explain.rule: This yellow direction panel (temporary roadworks sign) stands before a junction. Vehicles with an actual mass over 7 t going to Lucca may NOT go straight on (the 7 t ban is on the straight arrow) and must change route; lighter vehicles may go straight.
explain.trap: '7 metri di lunghezza' (7 metres long) is wrong: 't' means tonnes.

sceneParams.caption: 7 t = 7 tonnes, not 7 metres

q21901.en: The sign shown indicates the closure of the right lane because of roadworks.

explain.short: The red line is on the right and the right arrow bends left: the right lane closes for works.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'corsia di destra' (right lane): check the side of the red line, here the RIGHT.

sceneParams.caption: Right lane closed: move to the left lane

q21902.en: The sign shown indicates a reduction from two lanes to one.

explain.short: Two lanes at the bottom, only one after the red line: two lanes become one.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: Count the lanes: two, then one ('da due a una').

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes become one

q21903.en: The sign shown is placed near a roadworks site.

explain.short: It is a yellow temporary sign, used where works close a lane.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: Yellow = temporary works sign, so 'cantiere stradale' (roadworks site) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow sign = near roadworks

q21904.en: The sign shown can be completed with a panel showing the distance to the point where the lane closes.

explain.short: A small panel underneath can tell you how many metres away the lane closure is.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'può essere completato' (can be completed): an extra distance panel is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: A panel can show the distance to the closure

q21905.en: The sign shown indicates a narrowing of the carriageway because of roadworks.

explain.short: With one lane closed, the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles) gets narrower.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'restringimento' (narrowing): fewer lanes = narrower road.

sceneParams.caption: Lane closed = narrower carriageway

q21906.en: The sign shown indicates that you may overtake on the right.

explain.short: The right lane is closed: you cannot drive there at all, so you cannot overtake there either.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'sorpassare a destra' (overtake on the right) is wrong: the right lane is the one that closes.

sceneParams.caption: Right lane closes: no overtaking there

q21907.en: The sign shown announces an interchange where you can make a U-turn.

explain.short: The bending arrow means the lane ends and you merge left, not an exit for turning back.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'inversione di marcia' (U-turn) is wrong: the arrow just moves into the next lane.

sceneParams.caption: Lane merge for works, not a U-turn exit

q21908.en: The sign shown is found near a junction.

explain.short: It is placed near a worksite where a lane closes, not because of a junction.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'incrocio' (junction) is wrong: the place is a roadworks site.

sceneParams.caption: Placed before works, not a junction

q21909.en: The sign shown indicates a bus stop lay-by.

explain.short: The red line is a lane closed for works, not a stopping place for buses.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'fermata degli autobus' (bus stop) is wrong: nothing on the sign is about buses.

sceneParams.caption: Lane closed for works, not a bus stop

q21910.en: The sign shown indicates the closure of the lane for slow vehicles.

explain.short: It closes the normal right lane for works; it says nothing about a special lane for slow vehicles.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'corsia per i veicoli lenti' (slow-vehicle lane, an extra lane on climbs) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Right lane closed for works, not a slow lane

q21911.en: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles coming from the right.

explain.short: It is not a priority sign: it only shows that the right lane closes and the road narrows.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows that the RIGHT lane closes (red line) for works: two lanes become one and the carriageway narrows, so you move into the left lane. A panel with the distance to the closure can be added.
explain.trap: 'dare la precedenza' (give way) is wrong: the sign is about lanes.

sceneParams.caption: About lanes, not about giving way

q21912.en: The sign shown, placed where there are roadworks, tells each category of vehicle which lanes it may use.

explain.short: Cars are under both arrows, the lorry only under the right one: each category gets its lanes.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'categorie di veicoli' (vehicle categories): cars and lorries get different lanes.

sceneParams.caption: Cars: both lanes. Lorries: right lane only

q21913.en: The sign shown is used to indicate how the lanes are used.

explain.short: Each arrow is a lane, and the symbols under it show who may use it.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'uso delle corsie' (lane use) is exactly what this sign is about.

sceneParams.caption: Lane use sign for roadworks

q21914.en: The sign shown tells vehicles which lanes they must drive in.

explain.short: Lorries must use the right lane; cars may use both lanes.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'debbono circolare' (must drive): it is an obligation, not advice.

sceneParams.caption: Each vehicle must keep to its lanes

q21915.en: The sign shown tells lorries with a gross mass over 3.5 tonnes which lane they must use.

explain.short: The lorry symbol stands only under the right arrow: that is their lane.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'autocarri' (lorries): the lorry symbol means these heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries over 3.5 t: right lane

q21916.en: The sign shown indicates that lorries with a gross mass over 3.5 tonnes may only use the right lane.

explain.short: The lorry is drawn only under the right arrow, so lorries may use only that lane.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'solo la corsia di destra' (only the right lane): here the 'solo' is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries: right lane only

q21917.en: The sign shown indicates that you are approaching a motorway toll booth.

explain.short: It shows lanes for cars and lorries during works; it says nothing about a toll booth.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'casello autostradale' (toll booth) is wrong: there is no toll symbol here.

sceneParams.caption: Lane use during works, not a toll booth

q21918.en: The sign shown requires lorries to drive in parallel rows.

explain.short: Lorries get only ONE lane (the right one), so they cannot drive side by side in parallel rows.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'file parallele' (parallel rows, side by side) is wrong: lorries have a single lane.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries: one lane only, no parallel rows

q21919.en: The sign shown indicates that lorries must only overtake on the right.

explain.short: Lorries must stay in the right lane; the sign does not tell them to overtake on the right.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'sorpassare a destra' (overtake on the right) is wrong: the sign is about lanes, not overtaking.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries stay right; no overtaking on the right

q21920.en: The sign shown forbids motorcycles from using the left lane.

explain.short: Only lorries are limited to the right lane; motorcycles are not on the sign.
explain.rule: This yellow panel (temporary roadworks sign) shows lane use: cars may use both lanes, while lorries (autocarri) over 3.5 t must use only the right lane.
explain.trap: 'motocicli' (motorcycles) is wrong: the sign shows cars and a lorry.

sceneParams.caption: Only lorries are limited, not motorcycles

q21921.en: The delineators shown are used at the sides of the carriageway on one-way roads.

explain.short: Yellow reflectors mark the delineators for one-way roads, placed on both edges.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) matches the YELLOW reflectors.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow reflectors = one-way road edges

keywords.en: at the sides of the carriageway

q21922.en: The delineators shown are complementary signs.

explain.short: Delineators belong to the complementary signs (segnali complementari), which help you see the road layout.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'segnali complementari' (complementary signs) is the right family for delineators.

sceneParams.caption: Delineators are complementary signs

q21923.en: The delineators shown are placed at the edges of a one-way road or carriageway.

explain.short: Yellow delineators stand on the edges of a one-way road, or of one carriageway of a dual road.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'ai margini' (at the edges) and 'senso unico' (one-way): both are right.

sceneParams.caption: On the edges of a one-way road

q21924.en: The delineators shown help you see the course of the road better.

explain.short: A row of posts along the edge shows where the road goes, especially on bends and in the dark.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'andamento della strada' (course of the road): this is their main job.

sceneParams.caption: Posts show where the road goes

q21925.en: The delineators shown are placed on two-way roads.

explain.short: Yellow reflectors are for one-way roads; two-way roads use white and red reflectors.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso' (two-way) is wrong for YELLOW delineators.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow = one-way, not two-way

q21926.en: The delineators shown are found before a pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: Delineators run along the road edges; they do not announce pedestrian crossings.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento pedonale' (pedestrian crossing) is wrong: they mark the road edge.

sceneParams.caption: They mark road edges, not crossings

q21927.en: The delineators shown are placed in the middle of the carriageway.

explain.short: Delineators stand at the edges of the road, never in the middle.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'al centro' (in the middle) is wrong: they are at the edges ('ai margini').

sceneParams.caption: At the edges, not in the middle

keywords.en: in the middle of the carriageway

q21928.en: The delineators shown divide the carriageway into lanes.

explain.short: Lanes are divided by painted lines; delineators only mark the road edges.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'dividono ... in corsie' (divide into lanes) is wrong: that is the job of road markings.

sceneParams.caption: Lines make lanes; posts mark edges

q21929.en: The delineators shown are placed to mark a reserved parking area.

explain.short: They show the edges of a one-way road, not a parking area.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'area di sosta riservata' (reserved parking area) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Road edges, not a parking area

q21930.en: The delineators shown are visible only at night.

explain.short: You see the posts by day too; at night their reflectors shine in your headlights.
explain.rule: Delineators (delineatori: posts along the road edge) with YELLOW reflectors are used at the edges of one-way roads or one-way carriageways. They are complementary signs that show the course of the road, by day and especially in the dark.
explain.trap: 'solo di notte' (only at night) is wrong: day and night.

sceneParams.caption: Visible by day and by night

q21931.en: The delineators shown are useful above all when visibility is poor.

explain.short: At night, in fog or rain their reflectors show you where the road edge is.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'soprattutto' (above all) is right: it does not say 'only'.

sceneParams.caption: Most useful at night and in fog

q21932.en: The delineators shown are complementary signs.

explain.short: Delineators belong to the complementary signs (segnali complementari), which help you see the road layout.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'segnali complementari' (complementary signs) is the right family for delineators.

sceneParams.caption: Delineators are complementary signs

q21933.en: The delineators shown are placed at the edges of a two-way road.

explain.short: White and red reflectors are on the delineators for two-way roads, on both edges.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso' (two-way) matches the white and red reflectors.

sceneParams.caption: White/red = edges of a two-way road

q21934.en: The delineators shown help you see the course of the road better.

explain.short: A row of posts along the edge shows where the road goes, especially on bends and in the dark.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'andamento della strada' (course of the road): this is their main job.

sceneParams.caption: Posts show where the road goes

q21935.en: The delineators shown are useful only at night.

explain.short: They also help by day and in fog or rain, any time visibility is poor.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is wrong: also in fog, rain and by day.

sceneParams.caption: Not only at night: fog and rain too

q21936.en: The delineators shown are placed at least 100 metres from one another.

explain.short: Delineators stand at short, regular intervals so you see a row of them; on bends they are even closer.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'almeno 100 metri' (at least 100 metres) is wrong: they are closer together.

sceneParams.caption: Close together, not 100 m apart

q21937.en: The delineators shown are placed in the middle of the carriageway.

explain.short: Delineators stand at the edges of the road, never in the middle.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'al centro' (in the middle) is wrong: they are at the edges ('ai margini').

sceneParams.caption: At the edges, not in the middle

keywords.en: in the middle of the carriageway

q21938.en: The delineators shown divide the carriageway into lanes.

explain.short: Lanes are divided by painted lines; delineators only mark the road edges.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'dividono ... in corsie' (divide into lanes) is wrong: that is the job of road markings.

sceneParams.caption: Lines make lanes; posts mark edges

q21939.en: The delineators shown are placed at the sides of the carriageway on one-way roads.

explain.short: White and red reflectors are for two-way roads; one-way roads use yellow reflectors.
explain.rule: These white posts with a black band are normal delineators (delineatori) for TWO-WAY roads: red reflector on the right edge, white on the left edge. They are complementary signs at the road edges that show its course, useful above all in poor visibility.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) is wrong here: one-way delineators are YELLOW.

sceneParams.caption: One-way roads use yellow delineators

keywords.en: at the sides of the carriageway

q21940.en: The delineator shown is placed at the sides of one-way tunnels.

explain.short: This yellow panel lines the walls of one-way tunnels so you can see the tunnel's shape.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'gallerie a senso unico' (one-way tunnels) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow panels line one-way tunnels

q21941.en: The delineator shown is a complementary sign placed in one-way tunnels.

explain.short: It is a complementary sign, and its place is in one-way tunnels.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: Both parts are right: 'segnale complementare' and 'gallerie a senso unico'.

sceneParams.caption: Complementary sign for one-way tunnels

q21942.en: The delineator shown can also be found highlighting detours or narrowings of the carriageway.

explain.short: Besides tunnels, the same yellow panel can highlight a detour or a narrowing of the road.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): tunnels are its main use, but not the only one.

sceneParams.caption: Also used at detours and narrowings

q21943.en: The delineator shown is a complementary sign.

explain.short: Delineators, like this tunnel one, belong to the complementary signs (segnali complementari).
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'segnale complementare' (complementary sign) is the right family.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel delineator = complementary sign

q21944.en: The delineator shown is used to mark a one-way junction.

explain.short: It lines the sides of one-way tunnels; it does not mark a junction.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'incrocio' (junction) is wrong: tunnels, not junctions.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel sides, not a junction

q21945.en: The delineator shown indicates a closed road.

explain.short: It shows the edge of the road in a tunnel; traffic carries on.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'strada chiusa' (closed road) is wrong: it only marks the edge.

sceneParams.caption: Marks the edge; the road is open

q21946.en: The delineator shown is placed in the middle of the carriageway to mark an obstacle.

explain.short: It stands at the sides of the tunnel, not in the middle of the road as an obstacle marker.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'al centro' (in the middle) is wrong: it is at the sides ('ai lati').

sceneParams.caption: At the sides, not in the middle

keywords.en: in the middle of the carriageway

q21947.en: The delineator shown divides the carriageway into lanes.

explain.short: Lanes are divided by painted lines; this delineator marks the tunnel side.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'divide ... in corsie' (divides into lanes) is wrong: that is the job of road markings.

sceneParams.caption: Lines make lanes; this panel marks the side

q21948.en: The delineator shown is a distance panel placed near a level crossing.

explain.short: Level-crossing distance panels have red diagonal bars; this plain yellow panel is a tunnel delineator.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'pannello distanziometrico' (distance panel) is wrong: those have red bars.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel delineator, not a level-crossing panel

q21949.en: The delineator shown has its own light.

explain.short: It has no lamp: it is reflective and shines when your headlights hit it.
explain.rule: This all-yellow panel on a post is the tunnel delineator: it is placed along the sides of ONE-WAY tunnels. It is a complementary sign, can also highlight detours or narrowings, and is reflective (no light of its own).
explain.trap: 'luce propria' (its own light) is wrong: it only reflects light.

sceneParams.caption: Reflects your headlights, no own light
